proposal.name: Separate component evidence and bind its inputs

issue_plan.name: Separate component evidence and bind its inputs
issue_plan.summary: Three ordered plumbing changes complete issue #254: retain explicit declarations and check-input provenance, attribute independent supplied proof, conformance, runtime and assumption records, and render all of them safely in receipts. They preserve exact-target proof, legacy reports and fingerprints, and the refusal to execute explicit component checks; each change updates SPEC.md and README.md for what it ships, and the merger records the new evidence and assumption policy because plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Retain component declarations and all check-input provenance
issues.body:
Issue #254 extends the component evidence foundation for #244, the narrowed first step of #210. This first change supplies the declaration and input-snapshot foundation for independent evidence attribution. Today internal/project/components.go inventories scoped production Go files and resolves proof, test and conformance selections, but discards the snapshots of selected tests and drivers outside that scope. internal/verify/components.go copies only that production inventory into proof evidence and fingerprints, so editing an outside-scope driver is invisible. Fix that provenance gap without running checks or treating configuration as evidence.

Extend the optional components manifest configuration only for explicit target assumptions and reproducible invocation metadata. An assumption declaration names its target and has a stable identity, statement, reason/origin and source snapshot; permit a target whose only declarations are assumptions. Do not infer assumptions from source or instrument production code. Invocation metadata identifies the selected check and records the declarative information needed to reproduce an invocation, including ordered arguments, working directory, explicitly supplied environment or sampling parameters, and its input-file references as applicable. It is data, not an executable protocol: no shell evaluation, command launching, language adapter or runner is added. Keep existing manifests valid and existing canonical target/check IDs and selections intact.

Resolve selected test and conformance declarations into separate provenance containing their canonical IDs, full source-file hashes and declaration snapshots. Hash every explicitly declared execution input, including non-Go files such as fixtures, model dependencies, configuration and dependency manifests/lockfiles, rather than assuming that parsed Go declarations are all the inputs. Retain the module-file provenance used to resolve selected identities. Make this foundation capable of binding the model and ratified bounds and of comparing actual input snapshots supplied by the later attribution API with declared input snapshots. The API's callers will supply the actual execution inputs; discovery and declared invocation metadata alone cannot attest that a tool ran or that its input set was complete.

Keep this provenance separate from ComponentInventory.Files and ComponentInventory.Components, which continue to describe scoped production code. Merely selecting an out-of-scope driver or a test must not create a production component, inflate proof coverage, or invent a successful result. A driver that independently belongs to production scope still has its ordinary production row, with no inherited evidence. Preserve nonrecursive scope, every non-test Go file regardless of build tags, files without functions, unchecked neighbors, receiver-qualified and ordinal identities, and nearest-module identity resolution. Omitting components still returns the legacy inventory without new source discovery or required inputs.

Validate all new declarations and references during project loading/resolution. Reject unknown or duplicate selections, duplicate identities within their target/check namespace, duplicate input references, ambiguous declarations, missing required assumption/invocation data and nonexistent inputs. Input paths must obey the existing clean project-relative, regular-file and no-symlink boundary; reject absolute paths, traversal, aliases and escapes. Returned declarations and snapshots are canonical and detached from mutable caller-owned configuration. Inventory/configuration remains intent and contains no assurance or successful evidence.

Extend the existing proof-attribution inventory copying and fingerprint path to retain and bind these new declarations, associations, invocation metadata and input hashes. Bind complete production scope as before. Sort set-valued declarations, selections and file/input collections; preserve meaningful sequence order such as command arguments. Identical projects relocated to another checkout have the same IDs and fingerprints, and reordering declaration/selection metadata has no effect. Preserve existing volatile exclusions, including timestamps, build output, trace destinations, Go toolchain patch metadata and the coding agent; incidental checkout locations must not enter a fingerprint. Hash actual input-file bytes without weakening content identity. Keep successful legacy reports, Markdown, unverified-function lists and fingerprints unchanged.

Acceptance must use temporary projects and supplied data without real verifiers. Cover an assumption-only target remaining unproved, outside-scope selected tests/drivers recorded separately from production coverage, and edits to a selected driver, test, fixture, model/include and module/dependency input changing snapshots and fingerprints. Cover invocation/declaration changes, canonical order and relocation stability, caller mutation isolation, invalid paths including symlinks, unknown/duplicate declarations and references, and compatibility with the existing manifest and proof acceptance tests. Confirm no command is executed, verify.Check and verify.Run still return verify.ErrComponents before tools start, explicit Python/TypeScript configurations remain rejected, and verify.RunModel remains available.

Update SPEC.md and README.md in this change to describe the shipped declarations/provenance, the new fingerprint inputs and the continuing execution limit. Do not claim that independent result attribution or complete new receipt views have shipped in this step. Changed SPEC bullets cite their supporting decisions. The merger records the new declaration/assumption policy and any needed journal roll-up because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Ratified statements and locks remain unchanged.

Decisions: D-0013 (evidence from results), D-0024 and D-0029 (proof versus reproducible conformance), D-0082 (attempt coverage), D-0135 (agent excluded from fingerprints), D-0152 (ordinary-code components), D-0158 (explicit inventory and intent), D-0161 (successful evidence), D-0163 (exact-target proof and separate evidence), and D-0122 (current documentation).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Attribute independent component evidence without executing checks
issues.body:
Issue #254 extends the supplied-result component API for #244, the narrowed first step of #210. Build on the preceding merged declaration/input-provenance change: internal/project now retains explicit assumptions, selected check identities and separate snapshots for tests, drivers and declared execution inputs without adding production coverage rows. Extend internal/verify's report API and JSON representation to attribute independent proof, conformance, runtime-check and trusted-assumption records. This is an attribution and representation API for caller-supplied facts, not a verifier, runner, adapter, instrumentation system or gate connection.

Keep AttributeComponentProofs and its exact-target proof contract. A proof succeeds only for its configured target when the supplied result passed, names its verifier, has no errors, explicitly verifies that exact canonical target, covers every selected contract and has matching snapshots for every verified and checked-contract declaration. A helper, selected contract, same-named function or neighbor inherits no proof, even if named among the verified IDs of another target's result. Missing or incomplete proof stays unchecked. Preserve existing valid proof callers, including results that carry additional known verified declarations, checked contracts or input snapshots: these still confer coverage only on the selected target. Do not newly require invocation metadata for an otherwise valid existing proof-only call; when additional proof invocation/input provenance is supplied, validate and fingerprint it. Do not obtain new evidence from legacy package-level checks or discovered source.

Add independently attributable conformance records naming the exact configured target and selected canonical driver/check, runner/tool identity and pins, actual outcome, model identity and input snapshots, ratified bounds, sampled or bounded-exhaustive mode, observed run/step/state/transition counts and model state count, plus distinct attempt-coverage information. Carry reproducible invocation metadata and all actual execution inputs supplied by the caller, bound to the preceding foundation's snapshots. Successful sampled observations do not imply exhaustive coverage. An exhaustive-state claim requires supplied bounded-exhaustive mode, successful nonempty conformance, positive matching observed/model state counts and no failed attempt check, preserving D-0161. Keep the supplied mode even when the coverage claim must be qualified. Absent attempt coverage is not checked; only successful nonempty attempt-coverage evidence can establish every step tried. Preserve successful checked transitions separately from an unsuccessful attempt-coverage check, consistent with D-0082 and D-0161.

Add runtime evidence naming exact selected tests/checks, assertions actually exercised, runner/tool identity and pins, invocation/input snapshots, actual per-test and per-assertion outcomes, and diagnostics. A successful process or package test, a test name in configuration, or a legacy build result cannot imply that a target or assertion was exercised. Report only the tests and assertions supported by supplied outcomes; a target association expresses which check was selected, not inferred code coverage. This step adds no assertion discovery, production instrumentation or test execution protocol.

Add trusted-assumption records only for explicitly declared target assumptions. Retain declaration identity, exact target/source snapshot, statement and reason/origin, and always label them assumed/unverified. These are declarations rather than tool results: they cannot prove a component, count as a passed runtime/conformance check, complete missing contracts or attempts, or change the gate outcome. Require each supplied assumption to match its selected declaration; do not infer or silently invent assumptions or turn inventory alone into recorded execution evidence.

Unknown or duplicate references, unselected targets/checks and stale snapshots are attribution errors for every kind. New conformance/runtime/assumption records must reference their selected checks/declarations; retain the existing proof allowance for additional known declarations described above. Reject invalid batches atomically, including invalid records following valid ones. Require canonical IDs rather than bare names and matching source/contract snapshots. For the new executable kinds require matching selected invocation and declared input snapshots, plus matching model/bounds provenance for conformance. Actual execution inputs include the selected source plus every additional file supplied to the run, including non-Go data and model/dependency inputs. Well-formed unsuccessful or incomplete attempts can remain visible with diagnostics, but missing runner identity, missing inputs, no actual exercised checks, failed, timed-out, skipped or empty outcomes must never yield successful evidence; declarations and counts cannot substitute for actual outcomes. No result absent from the supplied data may be synthesized as a successful run.

Every attribution operation replaces or clears only the evidence kind it handles and preserves all other kinds, legacy checks, gate pass/fail, ratified data and model-only restrictions. Validate a detached candidate before committing it. When an operation supplies a replacement inventory, revalidate all retained kinds against its declarations, selections and snapshots: reject atomically if any retained evidence would become stale or unselected. In particular, an outside-scope driver edit must invalidate retained conformance when updating proof or runtime evidence, and a target/contract/input/assumption/model/bounds change must not be hidden by updating another kind. Canonically equivalent reordered inventories remain valid. The report owns deep copies of all nested collections. A successful update recomputes its fingerprint once for the resulting evidence.

JSON keeps the complete production inventory and lists every production component, including ones with no checks or results, with independent evidence kinds. Keep proof rows/statuses compatible with the existing API. A conformance-only or assumed neighbor remains unproved, and a component may simultaneously carry all four kinds without any score or aggregate proof label. CodeAssurance and Claim remain component evidence and EverySize remains false. Bind all declaration and selection identities, assumption contents/source, invocation metadata, model/bounds, all input hashes, outcomes, observations, attempt coverage and tool pins in canonical fingerprints. Preserve set/completion-order and relocation stability, meaningful argument order, existing volatile exclusions and successful legacy fingerprints/JSON behavior.

Acceptance uses supplied result records only. Exercise one target with all four independent kinds; a conformance-only neighbor and proof-contract helper with no proof; sampled and bounded-exhaustive observations with missing/failed/successful attempt coverage; runtime checks with actual assertions; and failed, timed-out, skipped, empty and missing attempts. Test unknown/duplicate/unselected/stale references and late batch failures with byte-for-byte unchanged report JSON and fingerprint on rejection. Attribute/update/clear kinds in different orders and verify preservation of other kinds, legacy checks and both gate outcomes. Test cross-kind stale inventory rejection in both directions, specifically driver-only edits, plus target/contract, test/input, invocation, assumption and model/bounds changes. Verify every new semantic input and outcome changes fingerprints, order and relocation do not, and mutating caller-owned nested values cannot change stored evidence. Retain all existing proof coverage and legacy compatibility checks, including valid proof-only calls without new invocation metadata and proof results with additional known declarations or checked contracts beyond the selection. With sentinel tools, confirm attribution launches nothing and explicit code verification still returns verify.ErrComponents before tools start; model-only behavior stays available.

Update SPEC.md and README.md for the shipped APIs, JSON, success rules, replacement/staleness semantics, fingerprint inputs and execution limit, citing supporting decisions on changed SPEC bullets. Correct the Report documentation and any explicit receipt/footer claim that all values come only from tools: explicit reports can now contain declared assumptions. Until the following presentation change renders all details, make the limited Markdown view clear rather than claiming it displays all new evidence; keep legacy rendering unchanged. The merger records the new evidence and assumption policy because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Do not edit ratified statements or locks.

Decisions: D-0013 (result-based evidence), D-0024 and D-0029 (proof and conformance), D-0082 (attempt coverage), D-0135 (fingerprint exclusions), D-0152 and D-0158 (ordinary-code components and explicit intent), D-0161 (successful evidence and bounded claims), D-0163 (exact-target proof, independent kinds and no score), and D-0122 (current documentation).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Render every component evidence kind safely in receipts
issues.body:
Complete issue #254's evidence representation for #244, the narrowed first step of #210, using the two preceding merged changes: explicit declaration/input provenance in internal/project and independent supplied-result attribution and fingerprinting in internal/verify. Extend internal/receipt's Markdown view and verify the JSON view so every production component and each separate evidence kind is visible. This completes the supplied-evidence API and receipts; component dashboard views belong to the surrounding #244 plan, and executable invocation protocols, language runners/adapters and gate connection remain with the later language-specific steps of #210.

List every production component, including unchecked neighbors, targets with no results and declarations used only as another target's proof contract. Display proof independently from conformance, runtime checks and trusted assumptions, allowing all kinds on one target. A conformance-only or assumed component must remain unchecked for proof. Retain exact component identities, source and contract hashes, selected checks, supplied outcomes and diagnostics. Include separate input-provenance details for selected tests/drivers and other execution inputs, with their identities and hashes, without converting them into production coverage rows. Configuration-only selections must be distinguishable from actual results, and missing results must not be fabricated.

Conformance presentation identifies the selected driver/check, runner and tool pins, model and ratified bounds, sampled versus bounded-exhaustive mode, observed counts and actual outcomes, and separately whether attempts were checked and what that check established. Keep exhaustive state coverage distinct from every step tried: positive matching state counts under successful bounded-exhaustive conformance and no failed attempt check can support exhaustive-state wording under D-0161, while every-step wording requires successful nonempty attempt coverage. Absent attempt coverage is visibly not checked; a failed attempt check qualifies exhaustive claims without erasing successful observations. Runtime presentation identifies the selected tests, assertions actually exercised, runner, outcomes and input provenance without inferring target coverage from a passing process. Unsuccessful, timed-out, skipped, empty and missing attempts never appear as successful evidence. Display assumption identity, target/source snapshot, statement and reason/origin as assumed/unverified declarations, visually and semantically separate from executable checks; they cannot receive pass/proved wording or contribute to success totals.

Keep explicit report claims at component evidence, with no aggregate assurance score, whole-project proof or every-size claim, and preserve the recorded gate outcome. The footer and surrounding prose must distinguish supplied tool outcomes from declared assumptions and must not say the explicit receipt is generated from tool output only. State the API's execution limit truthfully: these are supplied results/declarations and the API runs no tools. Preserve the legacy receipt path, including successful Go, Python and TypeScript Markdown bytes, fingerprints and unverified-function lists. New JSON fields remain optional for legacy reports; old proof-only explicit reports still render with new kinds absent, and decoding stale aggregate assurance labels cannot inflate component claims.

Render every source- or caller-controlled string safely using the existing component literal/text rules on each original value before assembling prose and markup. Cover assumption IDs, statements and reasons/origins; target/check/assertion identities; input paths and hashes; invocation metadata; model names, bounds and modes; runner/tool names and pins; outcomes and diagnostics; and the footer. Values containing HTML, Markdown links, automatic URLs, backticks, pipes, underscores, ampersands, literal entity text, CR or LF must remain inert text without adding links, HTML, table cells/rows or forged statuses. Preserve visible characters without double escaping, existing hash/digest shortening, original report/JSON values, gate result and fingerprint. Status wording is controlled by evidence semantics, never arbitrary supplied text.

Acceptance must construct reports through the supplied-result APIs without external verifiers, then check both JSON and Markdown. Include one target carrying independent proof, conformance, runtime and assumption records; a conformance-only neighbor; an unchecked helper used only as a proof contract; an assumption-only target; and no-result/failed/empty cases. Verify that all production rows are present, input-only drivers/tests add no coverage rows, each kind exposes its required provenance/outcome, failed attempt coverage cannot forge exhaustive-state claims and absent attempt coverage cannot forge every-step claims, and assumptions are always assumed/unverified including in the footer. Check legacy golden receipts/fingerprints and old proof-only JSON round trips.

Exercise hostile payloads throughout all new strings and assert their visible text and inert rendered structure, not merely a particular escape spelling. Check unchanged table/HTML structure and exact component/status associations, no active links or injected rows, no double escaping, and preservation of report JSON, fingerprint and gate outcome before and after rendering and JSON round trips. Existing explicit-receipt tests may need their intentional table/footer expectations updated, but retain their escaping, proof-attribution and identity assertions; do not weaken legacy golden checks. Finish end-to-end regression coverage for full input binding, outside-scope driver edits, canonical order/relocation, independent attribution preservation and cross-kind stale rejection using the preceding APIs. Run the relevant project/verify/receipt tests and the root Go test suite; no real runner integration is required for this supplied-data feature.

Update SPEC.md and README.md in this same change to describe the completed JSON/Markdown evidence API, assumption/tool distinction, complete input provenance, preservation and fingerprint rules, and the continuing verify.ErrComponents refusal before tools start. Remove the preceding step's temporary Markdown limitation and stale proof-only/future-evidence descriptions wherever they describe shipped behavior, including the roadmap descriptions. Explicit Python/TypeScript discovery remains rejected and verify.RunModel remains available. Changed SPEC bullets cite their supporting decisions; the merger records any remaining new evidence/assumption policy or journal roll-up because the build cannot write decisions/. Ratified statements and locks remain unchanged. No work needed to complete #254 is deferred beyond these three issues.

Decisions: D-0013 (receipts based on actual evidence), D-0024 and D-0029 (proof versus conformance), D-0082 (attempt coverage), D-0135 (provenance and fingerprint exclusions), D-0152 and D-0158 (ordinary-code components and inventory), D-0161 (claims from successful results), D-0163 (exact-target proof, separate kinds, escaped receipts and legacy compatibility), and D-0122 (current SPEC and README).

Kind: plumbing
